prompt: A tenant service account can read another namespace Secret while an admission webhook outage blocks unrelated deployments. Lead containment and recovery.
directAnswer: Declare credential/data exposure and API-write impact; freeze policy changes. Bind cluster, SA/token/Pod UIDs, audiences/expiry, audit IDs, exact Secret accesses, role/binding UIDs, webhook config UID/rules/selectors/timeout/failurePolicy and affected requests. Contain the workload/token, rotate exposed Secrets and preserve audit evidence. Trace cross-tenant grant through bindings/groups/aggregation/escalation and remove the smallest source grant. Separately restore or rollback the webhook through approved break-glass while retaining required security coverage; do not delete all admission. Verify tenant-required actions, cross-tenant Secret and workload actions denied, privileged dry-run denied, webhook latency healthy, rotated credentials used, user operation restored and cleanup/revocation proven.
foundation: A confidentiality breach and an admission availability failure are separate concurrent incidents.
seniorAnswer: I run two evidence streams under one incident command: data exposure containment and API-write recovery. I never solve webhook availability by silently removing the security boundary, and I never treat Pod deletion as credential revocation.
weakAnswer: Delete the Pod and all validating webhooks.
whyWeak: The token/grant and exposed data remain, while deleting all webhooks removes unrelated controls.

evidence.signal: rotated secret plus denied negative test

followUps.answer: Contain bound Pod/SA/grant, respect token lifetime and verifier behavior, rotate affected downstream credentials, and prove denial.
Only when predesigned risk policy permits that exact webhook/match; not ad hoc.
RBAC graph linting, tenant negative tests, webhook SLO/canary and break-glass drills.
